review_scope: Substantive offline review of native local JWT batch custody on frozen 02b; no Rust compilation, execution, Native or product changes.
conclusion: No concrete production security or Rust type/visibility blocker found in the reviewed three-file proposal and actual pinned dependencies. One meaningful regression proof gap must be corrected before claiming paired Auth/Namespace atomicity. Compile and real regressions remain mandatory.

required_test_correction.finding: The helper includes the old complete auth_mounts/jwt_mounts/tokens/root Identity projection plus batch_authority, but omits both the Auth namespace_batch_registry and the complete NamespaceRegistry. Its failure comparisons therefore cannot detect a standalone Namespace lifecycle change or ledger mismatch.
required_test_correction.minimal_fix: Retain all existing fields, add the complete serialized state.namespaces and the auth namespace_batch_registry value. Use existing bounded owner_store/secret serializer, private Zeroizing byte equality and erase_json; do not serialize EngineState or remove fields to make comparisons pass.

reviewed_boundaries.name: One verifier, fresh private witness
reviewed_boundaries.evidence: auth.rs c755af145c643bba143a0733459764bdb6fbd256: one verify_native_with_user_claim_and_lifetime branch; service.rs 2c850912c06599a46430d3cf59bda3f5b512b391 initializes authenticated_jwt_lifetime=None and exports only after finish_identity_response_observed succeeds. Native service candidate independently initializes jwt_lifetime=None; ownership uses take(). No second assertion verification was added.

reviewed_boundaries.name: Real Identity before sealing
reviewed_boundaries.evidence: service_identity.rs 3ecc61336c4678fe99b0224dce4650b1744e59d3 binds mount accessor/alias, checks disabled entity, binds actual issued entity and computes Identity policies before finish_pending_batch_observed. Auth batch finalizer 8142c4226a0fb6d9e010a3e52613ecc0c8a03e2e requires login entity, installs actual namespace binding, seals once and updates only candidate authority.

reviewed_boundaries.name: Closed batch claim inspection
reviewed_boundaries.evidence: auth_native_jwt.rs e082580797241ba4b57b3808e8a53f75ddcfece8 opens actual sealed batch through batch_principal_observed, validates root namespace/current namespace binding, no parent/origin/token-role/precision/CIDRs, exact role metadata/path/policies/expiry and same response entity, empty accessor/nonrenewable, no service-token backing row. Opening is batch authentication, not a second JWT assertion verifier.

reviewed_boundaries.name: Paired lifecycle and exact root delta
reviewed_boundaries.evidence: service_native_batch_lifecycle.rs 2e6b2df10e70aa0669ab27877fde75a1c5ad1068 prepares only a throw-away deterministic catalog; admit_domain_candidate checks original catalog/registry/root and candidate equality; admit_plan permits only exact Namespace ledger plus existing Auth/Identity delta. Candidate non-Identity engine changes remain rejected by native_namespace_identity_only_change.

reviewed_boundaries.name: Source and candidate eligibility
reviewed_boundaries.evidence: Both source and candidate still require root-only JWT mount/state, local config, valid user-claim/renewal/token graph and real origin markers. Added batch issuance validator checks existing authority and allowed typed mount state. The patch removes the service-only type guard without removing the retained JWT local/root, graph, renewal and public-origin constraints.

reviewed_boundaries.name: Expiry and original clock
reviewed_boundaries.evidence: Recomputed claims expiry uses the same source jwt_token_expiry function, role TTL/max/period and explicit cap calculated from actual signed-batch issued_at. Original NativeJwtLifetime from the JWT verifier is checked at bind, prepublication callbacks and post-audit reply. Existing RequestClock and OriginalDeadline are retained; no renewed deadline or JWT revalidation is added.

reviewed_boundaries.name: Delivery after audit
reviewed_boundaries.evidence: Before publication the exact JWT status/body digest is retained. Final complete_native_auth_delivery compares it and checks exact generation/checkpoint, original source Auth digest and warm NativeProof, current Auth and issued credential under original clock. Post-commit audit failure keeps the durable root and suppresses credentials; no rollback or automatic replay is claimed.

reviewed_boundaries.name: Rust shape and visibility
reviewed_boundaries.evidence: VerifiedBatchClaims getters exist in 7098a1b76c1d0b83414bf93697f0d24a1a052e28; auth sibling visibility permits all accessed pub(super) methods. The one bind_successful_login production call adds the matching origin_peer argument; no new public AuthResponse field or enum/provider variant. This is a source check only, not a successful compiler result.

namespace_snapshot_support.justification: The existing native lifecycle independently hashes the complete Namespace object and expects it unchanged at delivery; ordinary terminal Auth clock updates are already excluded by the old fixture projection. Durable workflow/catalog fields must remain included.

covered_source_paths: sealed stateless grants versus real service rows
bad signature and prepublication assertion expiry
forced batch and service period/use-limit semantics
limits: The proposed helper does not yet prove the paired Namespace invariants until required correction is applied.
New batch tests do not replace old source-clock/deadline/proof tests or imply HA, remote JWKS or child-namespace qualification.
No separate direct-batch role-deletion or mount-disable semantic claim is made by these six tests.
